_comment: Corrections to BODS's GTFS calendars where its conversion from the operators' own TransXChange is shown to be wrong. Applied by scripts/timetable_corrections.py inside scripts/build_timetable.py, only where the feed still shows the error's signature, so a fixed feed is left alone. Every change is logged and written to the timetable's corrections table, and a board on an affected day says so. Each entry carries its evidence, caveats, source and the feed it was checked against; `expires` is the last day it can matter.

corrections.summary: BODS's timetable data puts New Year's Eve on 1 December 2026, so 1 December loses its buses and 31 December keeps journeys the operators do not run. We move it back to 31 December.
corrections.evidence: Brighton & Hove's route 7 TransXChange for 29 November to 20 December and Stagecoach's two Coastliner 700 files (PK0002571-53 V31, PK0002571-116 V1) never mention 1 December; each excludes 13 holidays including NewYearsEve. BODS's GTFS calendars for them remove those holidays with 31 December replaced by 1 December (700 Monday to Friday calendar: 184 journeys in both). Across the south-east feed, of 313 calendars covering December that skip Christmas Eve, 268 also skip 1 December and 11 skip 31 December outside a school-holiday run (docs/reliability/bods_holiday_check.py). Brighton & Hove's own website shows a normal Tuesday service on 1 December. Services dated day by day (school days of Brighton & Hove, Metrobus, Compass and Stagecoach) lack 1 December inside otherwise unbroken runs of weekdays (30 November, 2 December, ..., 8 December), so that day is added back where the run is unbroken either side and a week later.
caveats: Shown from the operators' files for Brighton & Hove route 7 and the Coastliner 700; other operators' files were not all read.

A calendar whose 1 December exception sits beside exceptions on 30 November or 2 December is left alone, so a genuine one-off on 1 December inside a run of dates is not moved; an isolated genuine 1 December change would be.
What each operator runs on New Year's Eve evening is not established: this restores what their files say, no more.
A school service genuinely not running on 1 December (a training day), dated day by day with the days either side, would wrongly get it back. Not checked school by school.

corrections.summary: BODS's timetable data removes Christmas Day and New Year's Day from the calendars of services that run only on those days, so they never run. We put those days back.
corrections.evidence: Brighton & Hove's route 7 files for 20 to 26 December and 31 December to 2 January define a Christmas Day service (Friday, DaysOfOperation ChristmasDay) and a New Year's Day service (Monday and Friday, DaysOfOperation NewYearsDay). BODS's GTFS calendars for them (16612 and 18970) remove 25 December and 1 January, the only days they run. Brighton & Hove's website shows route 7 running on both days (144 and 808 times listed).
caveats: Only a calendar of at most 14 days that is left with no running day at all is changed, and only on 25 December or 1 January.

Both profiles also list ChristmasDayHoliday or NewYearsDayHoliday as non-operating; whether BODS misreads those or the operator's data contradicts itself is for BODS to say. The operator's website is the deciding fact.
